mission: Build Universal Round U.3 as the third universal-design layer for MathTeach, grounding neurodiversity-aware core design, trauma-informed but non-therapeutic safety, developmental and lifespan sequencing, and a stronger myth and anti-pattern catalog before disorder-specific support rules.
collection_principles: Treat neurodiversity-aware design as an early architectural default rather than a late accommodation layer.
Use trauma-informed principles only in bounded, non-therapeutic ways that improve safety, predictability, and dignity in tutoring.
Translate developmental and lifespan evidence into sequencing rules, not rigid stage stereotypes.
Maintain a strong myth and anti-pattern catalog so unsupported claims do not enter teacher policy.

domains.name: Neurodiversity-Aware Core Design
domains.goal: Make structure, pacing, representation, and friction reduction accessible by default before specific support profiles are activated.

domains.name: Trauma-Informed but Non-Therapeutic Safety
domains.goal: Build predictability, transparency, and non-shaming correction into tutoring without drifting into therapy.

domains.name: Developmental and Lifespan Sequencing
domains.goal: Help the tutor vary sequencing, abstraction, and pacing across children, adolescents, students, and adults.

domains.name: Myth and Anti-Pattern Catalog
domains.goal: Prevent learning-styles logic, neuromyths, deficit thinking, and badly timed minimal-guidance patterns from becoming defaults.

starter_sources.title: ADHD in the Classroom: Helping Children Succeed in School
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Official, practical anchor for early design implications around structure, feedback, transition cues, breaks, and reduced distraction.

starter_sources.title: Learning Disabilities
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Official overview for non-diagnostic, dignity-preserving framing of dyslexia, dysgraphia, and dyscalculia-relevant learning barriers.

starter_sources.title: Reading and Reading Disorders
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Useful core-design anchor for reading load, symbol-to-language load, and text-access issues that affect mathematics tutoring too.

starter_sources.title: Infographic: Does your child struggle with Math? Dyscalculia could be the reason.
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Early public-facing anchor for non-stigmatizing math-learning-disability framing and first-pass design awareness.

starter_sources.title: CAST Universal Design for Learning Guidelines 3.0
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Core design bridge for multiple means of representation, engagement, and action before special-case rules are added.

starter_sources.title: SAMHSA's Concept of Trauma and Guidance for a Trauma-Informed Approach
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Official anchor for bounded safety principles such as transparency, trustworthiness, choice, collaboration, and empowerment without turning the tutor into therapy.

starter_sources.title: How People Learn II: Learners, Contexts, and Cultures
starter_sources.organization: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Strong synthesis for developmental sensitivity, learner context, variation across learners, and the need to treat learning as context-embedded across stages.

starter_sources.title: The Adult Learner
starter_sources.date_label: classic andragogy line; current editions continue
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Brings the upper end of the lifespan explicitly into sequencing logic so adult learners are not treated as delayed schoolchildren.

starter_sources.title: Learning Styles: Concepts and Evidence
starter_sources.organization: Psychological Science in the Public Interest
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Core guardrail against converting learner preference claims into unsupported instructional policy.

starter_sources.title: Why Minimal Guidance During Instruction Does Not Work
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Foundational anti-pattern source against pushing novices into under-guided discovery before they have enough structure.

starter_sources.title: Neuroscience and Education: Myths and Messages
starter_sources.why_it_matters: Important guardrail against neuromyths being used as false justification for weak instructional or learner-model assumptions.
